as_told.title: Pilot Bud Clem follows a ball of light over Hanford

plain: In 1945, months before the first atomic bomb test in New Mexico and the bombings of Japan, glowing balls of light hovered over Hanford, the Washington state site making plutonium for the bomb, and jet fighters tried and failed to chase them away, according to the host. Michels tells it several times, crediting the researcher Robert Hastings and his book UFOs and Nukes and naming a pilot called Bud Clem as the witness, though once he credits a Lieutenant Commander Brown instead, and once he ties it to an Air Force study he calls Project Twinkle, which he says was deleted from the Air Force archives. He offers it as one of the earliest cases suggesting that something has been watching nuclear sites from the very start.
